stage1_hpo_curation.extraction_prompt_addendum: DSM-5-TR Major/Mild Neurocognitive Disorder (Chapter 16) is defined by ACQUIRED cognitive decline from a previous baseline in one or more of six domains. Map extracted human symptoms to these strict domains: (1) cognitive_executive - complex attention, executive function (planning, working memory, set-shifting, response inhibition, mental flexibility), and learning and memory (free recall, recognition, recent memory). Consolidates the attention/executive/memory poles into one domain. (2) motor_coordination - perceptual-motor function: coordination, gait, praxis, visuospatial navigation, and etiology-specific motor signs (parkinsonism in Lewy body / Parkinson disease, chorea and motor disorganization in Huntington disease, gait disorder in vascular / TBI). (3) social_cognition_empathy - recognition of others' emotions, theory of mind, empathy, social judgment; loss of empathy and social disinhibition are the behavioral-variant frontotemporal signature. (4) adaptive_functioning - Criterion B: interference with independence in everyday activities (instrumental activities of daily living). (5) neuropathology_progressive - the etiology-defining PROGRESSIVE neuropathology named by the subtype: amyloid and tau (Alzheimer), TDP-43 / tau (frontotemporal), alpha-synuclein (Lewy body / Parkinson), white matter / vascular injury, CAG-expansion degeneration (Huntington), spongiform change (prion). Tag the LANGUAGE domain (word-finding, naming, fluency, grammar) as 'other': language is a chapter-16 neurocognitive domain but has NO organism-level analog in the mouse, so it is not a strict NCD domain here. Extract phenotype FEATURES at the human-symptom level, not diagnoses. Do NOT extract from Differential Diagnosis or the delirium exclusion. The disorder-defining feature is PROGRESSIVE ACQUIRED decline; where the text marks progression or age-relatedness, set temporality accordingly. [2026-07-27 CRITERION-STRICT UPDATE: neuropathology_progressive is REMOVED as a face-validity domain; it is the etiology/pathology (mechanism axis), not a DSM Criterion A cognitive-decline criterion. Do NOT extract amyloid/tau/synuclein/pathology terms as scored NCD criteria -> other.]

stage2_rerank.developer_prompt_addendum: The 5 NCD strict domains: cognitive_executive (complex attention + executive function + learning/memory), motor_coordination (perceptual-motor, gait, parkinsonism, chorea), social_cognition_empathy (emotion recognition, empathy, social disinhibition), adaptive_functioning (Criterion B independence), and neuropathology_progressive (etiology-defining amyloid/tau/synuclein/vascular/CAG pathology). Mouse-proxy guidance: (a) cognitive_executive: impaired Morris water maze incl reversal, impaired novel object recognition, working-memory deficits (radial-arm, T-maze delayed alternation), 5-CSRTT attention, attentional set-shifting, go/no-go inhibition -> direct_analog/close_support; generic 'abnormal learning/memory/cognition' -> close_support. (b) motor_coordination: rotarod, beam walk, gait analysis, pole test, tremor, parkinsonian slowing/rigidity, chorea-like dyskinesia -> direct_analog/close_support. (c) social_cognition_empathy: observational-fear (Jeon 2010), consolation-like behavior, reduced social recognition/novelty preference -> close_support; the social component overlaps ASD -> disambiguation is downstream via disorder-specific gene evidence, not by inflating NCD strict-eligibility. (d) adaptive_functioning: nest-building (Deacon 2006 ADL proxy), burrowing, home-cage self-care -> close_support. (e) neuropathology_progressive: amyloid/tau/plaque/tangle, alpha-synuclein aggregation, TDP-43, neuronal loss, white-matter rarefaction, spongiform change -> direct_analog (this is a MECHANISTIC/pathology domain, positive-polarity: presence of pathology is the NCD-consistent direction). NCD NOTE: chapter-16 lines are overwhelmingly annotated by their PRIMARY neurodegenerative disease (AD, PD, HD, prion) rather than by a documented cognitive trajectory, so expect the neuropathology domain to carry most of the signal and the behavioral cognitive domains to be SPARSE. The acquired-decline-from-baseline event and the LANGUAGE domain have no mouse analog. Judge on construct merit; do not force cognitive analogs where only pathology is annotated. strict_eligible=true only for high-quality organism-level analogs (or, for neuropathology_progressive, high-quality pathology annotation).

diagnostic_ceiling.label: Major/Mild NCD requires decline in >=1 of six neurocognitive domains (A1-A6); modelled as 1-of-N over the strict domains present in mouse.

strict.name: cognitive_executive
strict.description: Cognitive deficits spanning learning, memory, attention, working memory, planning, set-shifting, response inhibition, reasoning, problem-solving, and cognitive flexibility. Consolidates cognitive_dysfunction (learning/memory pole) + executive_dysfunction (response-control pole). Mouse anchors: Morris water maze (Morris 1984), novel object recognition, 5-CSRTT (Robbins 2002), attentional set-shifting (Birrell & Brown 2000), reversal learning (Bissonette 2008), T-maze delayed alternation, puzzle box (Ben Abdallah 2011), go/no-go inhibition. NCD-specific anchor: Criterion A cognitive decline across complex attention, executive function, learning/memory.

strict.name: motor_coordination
strict.description: Perceptual-motor function — coordination, gait, postural control; etiology-specific motor symptoms (DLB parkinsonism, TBI gait deficits, vascular gait disorder). DSM-5-TR NCD Criterion A5. Mouse anchors: rotarod, beam walk, gait analysis (Brooks & Dunnett 2009), pole test.

strict.name: social_cognition_empathy
strict.description: Perspective-taking, recognition of others' emotional states, vicarious distress response, empathy-like behavior. Distinct from social_interaction (which is engagement/affiliation): this is the cognitive-social-processing dimension. Mouse anchors: observational fear (Jeon 2010 ACC-dependent), consolation-like behaviors, BTBR reduced empathy (Keum 2016), reduced reciprocal social novelty preference. NCD-specific anchor: Criterion A6 social cognition — recognition of others' emotions, social judgment, ToM proxies. Loss of empathy is bvFTD signature (Rascovsky 2011).

strict.name: adaptive_functioning
strict.description: Practical daily-living skills; self-care; functional independence in everyday activities. Maps to DSM-5-TR ID Criterion B and NCD Criterion B (interferes with independence). Mouse anchors: nest building scoring (Deacon 2006 as ADL proxy), burrowing, home-cage feeding-and-drinking competence. NCD-specific anchor: Criterion B interferes with independence in everyday activities (Major) or requires greater effort (Mild).

mechanism_axis.name: neuropathology_progressive_etiology
mechanism_axis.reported: separately from face validity; NOT in domains.strict and NOT in the discrimination composite
mechanism_axis.content: etiology-defining progressive neuropathology: amyloid/tau plaques and tangles (AD), TDP-43/tau (FTD), alpha-synuclein (DLB/PD), white-matter rarefaction (vascular), CAG-expansion degeneration (HD), spongiform change (prion), focal neuronal loss (TBI)
mechanism_axis.rationale: the etiology / 'due to X' pathology, NOT the DSM-5 Chapter 16 Criterion A cognitive-decline diagnostic criterion; the exact analog of SCZ's salience substrate (a mechanism domain that would prop up a disorder whose criteria are hard to model). Reversed the earlier decision that admitted mechanistic evidence to strict for NCD.
